Category.description: Found each district with an economic role, a social character and at least one trait. Ordinary is exclusive. Every other trait shapes conditions across the district throughout development. Existing evidence favors compatible draws and earlier selections progressively discourage repeats.

Name.description: Generic catalog name for a repeatable economic role, social character or trait. Each district also has its own generated or retained place name.

Localized origin.description: For traits whose character can be traced to a particular source or home. The origin is district detail. It does not commission a POI or define the reach of the effect.

items.Composition interactions: The economic and social programs alone shape this district.
items.Core idea: The district has its economic role and social character without an additional trait effect.
items.Eligibility requirements: Available to every newly founded district.
items.Generative effects: Adds no site or land-use influence and ends the trait draw.
items.Name: ordinary
items.Provenance: Owner direction, 2026-11-25.
items.Weighted suitability: Uses the city's ordinary weight and the same growing repeat penalty as other traits.

items.Composition interactions: Crowded-tenement society can make a tight night bazaar, patrician society can build guarded merchant courts, newcomers can run culturally distinct exchanges; optional Veil/ruin/animal traits rearrange access, stalls, safety and specialized goods only when sourced.
items.Core idea: A theatrical fantasy market quarter where caravans, guild factors, haggling merchants and auctioneers compete for valuable frontage and public trading ground; ordinary exchange is always possible, rare/exotic goods require real suppliers.
items.Eligibility requirements: Available to occupied districts. Trade and arriving routes favor a market.
items.Generative effects: Markets favor trade frontage and principal approaches. A bargaining court, covered bazaar or commodity yard can express that role at a specific site.
items.Name: grand bazaar
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Trade turnover raises the draw weight, especially where routes bring arrivals.

items.Composition interactions: Patrician estates create elite patron-backed workshops, warrens create dense small makers, guild society shares machines and service courts; ruins supply reused materials and Greenwood/creature traits alter workshop upkeep or siting.
items.Core idea: A district of smiths, masons, dyers, glassworkers, tinkers or fantastical artificers, producing visible craft specialization from actual workers, materials and machinery rather than generic 'shops.'
items.Eligibility requirements: A district can establish workshops. Craft traditions, materials and power favor them. Magical crafts depend on their medium.
items.Generative effects: Workshop ground and access for workers and deliveries gain weight. Forge courts, dye channels and loading passages are possible local expressions where the craft has materials and access.
items.Name: artificer quarter
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Craft activity and available capital together favor workshops.

items.Composition interactions: Guild commons can manage tolls and warehouses, patricians may privatize quays, warrens crowd behind dock walls; old walls and Veil discontinuities produce distinctive choke points without invented cargo or portals.
items.Core idea: The noisy transfer ward for caravans, pack beasts, cargo boats and heavy freight, with guarded arrival courts and goods moving between transport modes.
items.Eligibility requirements: Arriving routes and existing trade favor the formation of freight yards.
items.Generative effects: Freight favors trade frontage, working yards and high-access approaches. A freight yard may take the form of a caravanserai, weighing house or stock pen. Quays require a suitable shore.
items.Name: caravanserai and quays
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Arriving routes carry more weight where trade is already active.

items.Composition interactions: Warrens produce packed food stalls and tenement bakehouses, patrician estates sponsor walled granaries and provision gardens; beast rookeries, springs, floods and old walls change sanitation, storage and access.
items.Core idea: The city's food-making underbelly: millers, butchers, bakers, brewers, fishmongers and grain factors, fed by real rural or imported supply rather than a generic food-services label.
items.Eligibility requirements: Cultivated land and approaches favor food storage and provisioning.
items.Generative effects: Provisioning favors working ground, gardens and access. Granaries, mills, ovens and produce markets are possible local expressions.
items.Name: granary quarter
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Provisioning and access from arriving routes favor a granary quarter.

items.Composition interactions: With exiles the hostel becomes an arrival neighborhood; with patricians it becomes fashionable bathhouses and guest compounds; with crowded warrens it becomes cramped lodging and shared kitchens. A famous resident or haunted ruin changes who visits.
items.Core idea: A fantasy city's living hospitality district: inns, bathhouses, boarding halls, healers, hostels, cooks and small household trades serve locals, travelers and the unlucky.
items.Eligibility requirements: Available to every occupied district. Dense housing and arrivals favor services.
items.Generative effects: Hospitality favors housing, neighborhood trade and access. Inn courts, communal kitchens, stables and bath grounds are possible local expressions.
items.Name: inn quarter
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Built ground, crowding and arrivals favor household services.

items.Composition interactions: Guild governance produces schools and craft patents, patricians private salons, warrens cheap copyists' alleys, ruins archive-hunting scholars, and an actual Veil/Salt/Aurora phenomenon may change studies without authoring new magic.
items.Core idea: An enclave of scribes, astrologers where supported, cartographers, physicians, apothecaries, tutors and archive keepers, whose patronage and knowledge can physically dominate a district.
items.Eligibility requirements: A district can establish schools or scriptoria. Investment, wealth and existing seats of learning favor them.
items.Generative effects: Learned services favor civic ground, gardens and housing. A scriptorium, herb garden, archive court or medical hall can express those uses locally.
items.Name: scribe and apothecary quarter
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Standing investment and relative wealth favor learned services.

items.Composition interactions: Grand Bazaar yields bazaar-warrens; Scriptoria supports cramped copyist lodgings; the old city wall may confine or divide houses; creatures, floodwater and Greenwood create distinct burdened or celebrated warrens.
items.Core idea: An iconic crush of tightly inhabited courts, improvised additions, shared resources and contested passage: a social morphology of crowding, not an automatic morality or crime label.
items.Eligibility requirements: Available across occupied districts. Crowding and modest household capital favor tenements.
items.Generative effects: Housing gains ground and the district places less demand on principal approaches. Shared courts, narrow service passages and closely spaced dwellings are possible local expressions.
items.Name: tenement warrens
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Crowding raises the weight most where capital and relative wealth are modest.

items.Composition interactions: Freight gives private merchant dynasties and warehouses, Scriptoria gives patronized scholars, arts/crafts give luxury workshops; ruins or Veil hazards become private guarded landmarks rather than vanishing.
items.Core idea: A landscape of powerful families, luxurious estates, controlled gates, retainers and rival household compounds—where actual status or patronage can afford visible space.
items.Eligibility requirements: Available across occupied districts. Relative wealth, standing and lower density favor reserved estates.
items.Generative effects: Estates favor extensive gardens and reduce demand for through access. Private gardens, long approaches and open ground between compounds are possible local expressions.
items.Name: noble estates
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Relative wealth and capital favor estates. Crowding reduces that advantage.

items.Composition interactions: Bazaar + Guildholds becomes competing auction halls, Freight becomes a convoy league, Food yields bakers' and millers' guild courts; old ruins and fantastical traits can change oaths, shared equipment and property rules without free magic.
items.Core idea: Corporations and brotherhoods govern shared courtyards, negotiated rights and collective services under binding charters or guild oaths.
items.Eligibility requirements: Local makers and cooperative production favor the formation of a guild commons.
items.Generative effects: Makers favor workshop ground, common land and civic investment. Shared work courts, guildhalls and common machinery are possible local expressions.
items.Name: guild commons
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Local craft activity raises the weight of a guild commons.

items.Composition interactions: Outlanders trading in a bazaar generate diplomatic markets, artisans carry skills, innkeepers receive pilgrims; economic wealth and actual inherited rights determine whether it is elite, cramped or communal. A famous NPC could anchor an existing refuge.
items.Core idea: An arrival community of refugees, migrants, traveling peoples or exiles maintaining distinct customs, meeting places and internal routes, sometimes wealthy, sometimes struggling, never automatically a ghetto.
items.Eligibility requirements: A ward can establish a newcomer community. Trade and contacts favor its settlement.
items.Generative effects: Newcomer households favor housing, common ground and local trade. Guest markets, threshold squares and family courts are possible local expressions.
items.Name: outlander enclave
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Arrivals and trade turnover together favor the founding of an enclave.

items.Composition interactions: An artisan Freefolk ward shares workyards, a market quarter bargains over stall rights, a freight ward controls public tolls; a spring or ancient ruin can become a protected communal site and an outgrown wall a shared promenade.
items.Core idea: A self-governing ward of independent households, mutual defense and open commons, held together by assemblies, charters or hard-won freedoms rather than wealth or aristocratic patronage.
items.Eligibility requirements: Households can found a free commons. Shared tenure and farmland favor the draw.
items.Generative effects: Shared tenure favors common ground, housing and access. An assembly green, shared mill or public meeting hall can express common tenure locally.
items.Name: freehold commons
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Free households or common tenure raise the draw weight. Food production also favors a commons.

items.Composition interactions: A bazaar gains peculiar unloading/inspection courts if a real stable connection exists; the Warrens crowd around hazardous shortcuts; Highborn Courts may gate dangerous ground. Do not author a new Veil link or practitioners from a trait selection.
items.Core idea: A rip, fold, unreachable near-place or unstable seam in the Veil is woven through the district's daily routes, fortunes and fears; only real, maintained paired doors enable reliable passage.
items.Eligibility requirements: An existing Veil medium or retained discontinuity supports this trait. Known crossings can inform the district.
items.Generative effects: Across the ward, disturbed ground discourages through movement. Reliable approaches gain trade and waiting space. Existing Veil doors retain their own geography and rules.
items.Name: Veil-frayed streets
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: A local Veil medium or a matching known feature makes the trait eligible. Arriving routes increase its weight.

items.Composition interactions: Freefolk can protect sacred/public groves, guilds bargain for access, and a merchant quarter may lose or gain an intimate covered arcade. Actual Greenwood media and rooted vegetation must be the cause.
items.Core idea: An old quarter is being entangled, sheltered or consumed by Greenwood growth that competes with stone, roofs and human tenure.
items.Eligibility requirements: An existing Greenwood medium or established sign of encroachment supports the draw. Tree cover and wet ground shape its local expression.
items.Generative effects: Encroachment increases pressure for shared green ground and gardens and makes routes through rooting ground more costly. Expression varies with canopy, water and local Verdure.
items.Name: Greenwood encroachment
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: A local Greenwood medium or a matching known feature makes the trait eligible. Tree cover increases its weight.

items.Composition interactions: Scriptoria copy testimony, guilds maintain shrines and patricians defend family crypts; a crowded market may press against sacred empty land, but no dead are raised and no new Salt field is created.
items.Core idea: Preserved ancestors, bone courts and record-keeping funerary custodians sit beside the living, changing rights to some of the city's most valuable ground.
items.Eligibility requirements: Burial customs can form across a district. Existing burial grounds favor the draw. Magical preservation requires actual Salt.
items.Generative effects: Funerary custom preserves communal burial ground and favors civic stewardship and processional access, particularly through older masonry and inhabited streets. Existing ossuaries may bear witness to the custom.
items.Name: ancestral burial traditions
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Standing capital and existing burial evidence favor the custom.

items.Composition interactions: Tenement residents improvise elevated commons while wealthy courts fund raised approaches; a freight district moves loading toward deeper shore. Do not conjure a flood on dry high ground or replay global erosion.
items.Core idea: The quarter lives with recurring water, silt and drowned former streets; practical boats, raised thresholds and abandoned lower levels become common where hydrology supports them.
items.Eligibility requirements: Wet and low-lying land favors exposure across the district. Dry approaches can carry diverted traffic.
items.Generative effects: Low wet lanes favor open ground, gardens and diversion of through traffic. Dry approaches become more attractive throughout the district. The existing river and floodplain retain their courses.
items.Name: flood-prone lanes
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Wet ground raises the weight of flood exposure.

items.Composition interactions: Guildholds may meter water, Freefolk protect a commons, noble families enclose gardens, and food makers establish viable mills only with sufficient flow. A magical blessing is optional and requires genuine magical evidence.
items.Core idea: An actual perennial source of water becomes a fiercely valued district heart, treasured as a blessing whether or not it possesses any magic.
items.Eligibility requirements: District water use and gardens can develop around a retained or locally generated source.
items.Generative effects: Reliable water encourages gardens, shared land and accessible approaches across the district. An identifiable water source can be recorded as its origin.
items.Name: spring-fed district
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Wet ground favors a spring. An existing matching source adds support.

items.Composition interactions: Markets may use a vault entrance, residents build over older masonry and scholars seek records. Reuse retained remains where available.
items.Core idea: Older ruins persist as steps, crypt vaults, buried lanes and reused halls beneath an occupied quarter, making present streets follow inconvenient ancient stone.
items.Eligibility requirements: Older foundations can persist under inhabited land. Local ruins and established settlement favor their reuse.
items.Generative effects: Older building strata influence access, civic stewardship and open courts throughout inhabited ground. Where ruined masonry survives, its influence is stronger.
items.Name: built over ruins
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Ruined stock favors the reuse of older foundations.

items.Composition interactions: Gate passages draw traffic. Fragments can reserve land or survive as a common walk inside the growing city.
items.Core idea: Older defense rights can shape common walks and frontage inside the present settlement. Physical wall sections belong to the defense process.
items.Eligibility requirements: Settlement can preserve the rights of way and common land of an earlier enclosure. Surviving defenses provide evidence.
items.Generative effects: Inherited rights of way and shared ground affect circulation, common walks and working frontage. Surviving sections strengthen these effects along their alignments. Defense owns physical walls and gates.
items.Name: former walled quarter
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Developed ground and evidence of former defenses favor this trait.

items.Composition interactions: A resident and their home give nearby markets customers, workshops commissions and the district a named destination.
items.Core idea: A patron’s household brings visitors, trade and civic influence throughout the district. Their home can be recorded in finer detail.
items.Eligibility requirements: A district can establish a notable resident, their role and home. Their visitors and patronage affect commerce and access across the district.
items.Generative effects: Visitors and patronage draw commerce and civic investment across the district, especially on accessible frontage. District detail can identify the person, their livelihood and their residence.
items.Name: patronage of a notable resident
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Relative wealth favors the rise of a patron. Evidence of an existing resident adds support.

items.Composition interactions: Forgeways may dislike heat-loving beasts, the Warrens shelter from swarms, Highborn Courts keep display roosts and Freefolk protect a nesting green. Species, breeding and habitat remain controlled by ecology, not selected out of thin air.
items.Core idea: A spectacular rookery, den or herd of real native or fantastical creatures occupies city cliffs, towers, warm chimneys or sacred treetops, to residents' delight or fury.
items.Eligibility requirements: Trees, steep ground and occupied rooftops support nesting throughout a district.
items.Generative effects: Nesting influences the use of trees, rooftops and steep ground across the district. Shared habitat competes with construction and through access near suitable nesting areas.
items.Name: nesting colonies
items.Provenance: Introduced in the Phase 5 district catalog and used by the City district selector.
items.Weighted suitability: Tree cover and built ground favor nesting colonies.
